items.label: Industry: US Oil Refining
items.detail: Selected via account-grounded holdings: the IBKR connector was authenticated this session, and the account directly holds MPC (Marathon Petroleum, 6 sh, $2,730.18 market value, +$327.98 unrealized, bought 2026-09-14 at $400.20 off a 2026-09-07 Momentum HIGH call at $370.72). 2026 has been a historic year for US refiners: Marathon, Valero, and Phillips 66 together earned roughly $12.6B in Q2 2026 (their highest combined quarterly result since 2022) as Strait of Hormuz tension and attacks on Russian refining capacity tightened global product supply -- USGC 3-2-1 crack spreads reached ~$41.75/bbl in April 2026 (+95% YoY) and MPC's own refining margin more than doubled to $36.33/bbl. The tailwind is also structural, not purely cyclical: EIA's January 2026 Refinery Capacity Report shows operable US atmospheric distillation capacity down ~1% YoY to 18.2 million b/cd across 130 refineries (two fewer than 2025), no new US refinery has been built since the 1970s, and demand has exceeded capacity by roughly 400,000 bpd on average since 2023. Not covered by any prior scout cycle (critical minerals 2026-08-31, GLP-1 2026-08-31, gaming 2026-09-06, search/ads/cloud 2026-09-13, nuclear/SMR 2026-09-20, neoclouds 2026-09-27, beauty & personal care retail 2026-10-04).

items.label: MPC
items.detail: Marathon Petroleum -- held, 6 sh, $2,730.18 market value (+$327.98 unrealized), bought 2026-09-14 at $400.20 off a 2026-09-07 Momentum HIGH call at $370.72; now $455.04 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-11), +13.7% since entry and +22.8% since the original call price. Reinforcing evidence this cycle: Q2 2026 refining & marketing margin more than doubled YoY to $36.33/bbl as the Strait of Hormuz disruption and Russian refinery outages tightened global product supply, and the stock returned +55.1% in Q3 2026 alone -- the best of the three US majors (PSX +51.8%, VLO +49.4%), per sector performance coverage. Real risk, not glossed over: MPC is trading just 3.2% off its 52-week high of $469.91 after that run, so most of the re-rating from the supply shock is already in the price, and analysts explicitly caution that refining margins move with crack spreads, which can narrow quickly -- this is a cyclical tailwind riding on top of the structural capacity story, not a guaranteed continuation.

items.label: VLO
items.detail: Valero Energy -- not held. The largest independent US refiner and the cleanest way to extend the same crack-spread tailwind lifting MPC, with added diversification into renewable diesel through its Diamond Green Diesel joint venture (with Darling Ingredients) -- one of the largest renewable diesel platforms in the US, positioned to benefit from the EPA's finalized 2026-2027 RFS rule raising the 2026 biomass-based diesel volume to 8.86B gallons (+24.4% vs. the original proposal). Stock last $434.80 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-11), within 3.3% of its 52-week high of $449.65 after a +49.4% Q3 2026 return -- entering here means buying into a rally that has already largely happened, not getting ahead of it.
items.diversification_note: Refiner economics are driven by the crude-to-product crack spread rather than crude price itself, so VLO's correlation to the account's existing crude/commodity beta (DBC, FCX, CCJ) is complementary rather than redundant -- refiners can do well even when crude prices are flat or falling, as long as product demand holds and capacity stays tight.
items.suggested_size: Starter position given the stock is already near its 52-week high; a pullback toward the 13-week low ($286.53) would offer a materially better entry on the same thesis.

items.label: PSX
items.detail: Phillips 66 -- not held. The most diversified of the US majors (refining + midstream + chemicals), which smooths crack-spread cyclicality relative to a pure-play refiner, and the only one of the three actively expanding footprint rather than just riding margins: Phillips 66 Limited agreed in January 2026 to acquire the Lindsey Oil Refinery assets in the UK (113,000 bpd) to fold into its Humber refinery, adding scale without adding a new standalone competitor. Stock last $278.00 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-11), 2.9% off its 52-week high of $286.48 after a +51.8% Q3 2026 return -- same late-cycle entry-price caveat as VLO.
items.diversification_note: The midstream/chemicals mix gives PSX a different risk profile than a pure refiner -- less upside torque when crack spreads widen, but less downside torque if they narrow -- which pairs differently with the account's higher-beta commodity names than a pure-play refiner would.
items.suggested_size: Starter position for the same late-cycle-entry reason as VLO; the diversified earnings base makes it the lower-beta way to add refining exposure into strength.

items.label: DINO
items.detail: HF Sinclair -- not held. A smaller, Rockies/Mid-Continent-focused refiner with the most direct renewable-fuels torque in the group: Q2 2026 renewables adjusted EBITDA swung to +$123M from -$2M a year earlier on higher RIN prices and Producer's Tax Credit benefits, while core refining adjusted EBITDA more than doubled to ~$1.02B from $476M. Management raised the quarterly dividend 5% to $0.525 and is moving to spin off its lubricants unit, both signals of confidence in the cash-flow outlook. Real risk: HF Sinclair is suing the EPA over delayed biofuel-blending decisions, and the renewables upside is itself a bet on RIN prices staying near their 2021 all-time highs ($2.41 D4 / $2.37 D6 as of early June) -- a policy-sensitive tailwind, not a durable moat. Stock last $121.45 (IBKR snapshot, 2026-10-11), just 2.2% off its 52-week high of $124.17.
items.diversification_note: Inland Rockies/Mid-Continent crude sourcing and the renewables segment give DINO a different margin driver than the Gulf Coast majors (MPC, VLO, PSX), reducing overlap within a refining allocation rather than stacking the same regional exposure three times.
items.suggested_size: Starter position; the renewables segment's dependence on RIN price levels makes this the highest policy-risk name of the three majors-and-near-majors covered here.

items.label: PBF / DK / CVI (small-cap independent refiners)
items.detail: PBF Energy, Delek US, and CVR Energy -- not held, grouped because none individually clears the bar for a standalone call yet but all three show the same pattern: high operating leverage to the crack-spread cycle, real balance-sheet repair underway, and stocks already up sharply (PBF last $84.85, 5.1% off its 52-week high of $89.48; Delek last $74.51, 9.3% off its 52-week high of $82.12; CVR last $58.02, 5.0% off its 52-week high of $61.09 -- IBKR snapshots, 2026-10-11). PBF targets $350M in run-rate cost improvement by year-end 2026 from its RBI reliability program; Delek raised its Enterprise Optimization Plan target to $220M in annual run-rate improvements after Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA of $211.7M, well above the year-ago quarter; CVR beat Q1 2026 consensus (-$0.04 actual vs. -$0.58 expected). Smaller scale and higher leverage make these the names most likely to get acquired if the cycle turns and majors look to add capacity cheaply (Marathon's own history includes a $35.6B Andeavor takeover) -- worth tracking for both a cyclical re-rating and a possible consolidation premium, but not yet a specific call.

items.label: RFS/RIN compliance cost burden
items.detail: No specific ticker -- a sector-wide regulatory cost sitting under every refiner in this report. The EPA's finalized 2026-2027 Renewable Fuel Standard volumes (March 26, 2026) raised the 2026 biomass-based diesel obligation to 8.86 billion gallons, 24.4% above the original June 2025 proposal, while D4 and D6 RIN prices climbed to $2.41 and $2.37 respectively (as of June 4) -- near their 2021 all-time highs. AFPM estimates the RFS mandate could cost refiners over $106 billion over two years at current RIN price levels, and S&P Global reports D4 RIN generation reached only 43% of the full-year obligation by midyear, meaning refiners may need to draw down banked RINs or throttle gasoline supply to stay in compliance. This cuts two ways across the names covered here -- a direct cost for refiners without renewable-fuel capacity, but a profit driver for those with renewables segments (DINO's RIN-driven renewables EBITDA swing, VLO's Diamond Green Diesel JV) -- so it's worth tracking RIN prices and each company's blending-obligation coverage each quarter rather than assuming it hits the group uniformly.

items.label: Crack-spread cyclicality and Strait of Hormuz de-escalation risk
items.detail: No specific ticker -- the central risk under this entire industry thesis. The 2026 refining boom is substantially a supply-shock story: Iran/Strait of Hormuz tension and attacks on Russian refining capacity have curtailed global product flows, pushing USGC 3-2-1 crack spreads to ~$41.75/bbl in April (+95% YoY) and driving the sector-wide stock rallies covered in this report (MPC +55.1%, PSX +51.8%, VLO +49.4% in Q3 2026 alone). Every name discussed here is trading within single digits of its 52-week high on the back of this. S&P Global's own coverage cautions explicitly that refining profits move with crack spreads, which can narrow quickly -- a resolution or de-escalation of the Hormuz/Russia disruptions, a demand-side recession shock, or a wave of OPEC+ supply returning to market would each compress margins fast and hit every name in this report simultaneously, not selectively. Worth tracking via crack-spread data (RBN Energy, EIA STEO) each cycle rather than treating it as a stock-specific risk.
